brief.situation: 12:15, the dining room of a nursing home. You are the nurse aide on the floor at lunch. Mr. Rossi, 81, sits at your table: regular diet, feeds himself, mild memory loss, no swallowing restrictions in the care plan. Full code (no DNR order).
handover: Care plan: set up the meal, cut meat into small pieces on request, encourage him to sit upright and eat slowly.
The nurse is at the medication cart in the hallway.
Facility policy: shout for help or use the overhead call; the nurse activates the emergency response and calls 911.
howItWorks: The clock runs in real time at the pace you choose: study pace (3x) or exam realism (1x). Pause any time.
Your actions are a nurse aide's: watch, ask, call for help, back blows and abdominal thrusts, CPR, report and write it down. No medicines or orders.
Each set of back blows, thrusts or compressions takes as long as it would at the table.
Early on you are asked to write what you would do. Then a debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Mr. Rossi starts coughing 30 s into lunch.
The cough stops working 45 s later: severe obstruction.

Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. He becomes unresponsive after about 100 s with no air moving. whatNow.question: Mr. Rossi is coughing hard and says something went down the wrong way. What do you do now, and what would make you act differently?

parts.label: Now
parts.criteria: Stays with him and encourages him to keep coughing because forceful coughing with speech means air is moving (mild obstruction); does not give back blows, abdominal thrusts, water or a finger sweep while he can cough and speak; watches him closely.
parts.modelAnswer: He can cough and talk, so air is moving: stay with him, encourage him to keep coughing and watch him. No back blows, thrusts, water or finger in the mouth while he can cough.

parts.label: If it changes
parts.criteria: Names at least two signs of severe obstruction (cannot speak, silent or weak cough, cannot breathe, hands at the throat, blue lips) and the response: shout for help and activate the emergency response while staying, then cycles of 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until it comes out; CPR if he becomes unresponsive. Stays within the aide's role (no medications or orders).
parts.modelAnswer: If he can't speak or cough, or turns blue with his hands at his throat, that is severe: shout for help so the nurse and emergency team come while I stay, then 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts, again and again until it comes out. If he goes limp, lower him to the floor and start CPR, looking in his mouth before breaths and taking out only what I can see.

expertPath.text: He coughs hard and can talk: ask, stay, encourage the cough, watch.
Silent, hands at his throat, lips blue: ask 'Are you choking?' (he nods), shout for help so the nurse and emergency team come, and stay.
5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts, then back blows: the food comes out about 30 s after the airway closed.
Nurse arrives: report what you saw, what you did and how he is now in objective words, then write the note.

safe.headline: Cleared while awake, help called, reported
safe.body: You let the cough work, recognized the moment it stopped working, called for help without leaving, and used the 2025 sequence. That is the expert path.

breathingAgain.headline: Breathing again, by a harder route
breathingAgain.body: He is breathing, but it took longer than it needed to or he lost consciousness on the way. Look at the seconds after the cough went silent: shout, stay, 5 back blows and 5 thrusts.

anoxic.headline: Too long without air
anoxic.body: The most useful kind of run to learn from. Find the moment the cough went silent, and what shouting for help and starting back blows right then would have changed.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: He was breathing, but the report or the note never happened. A resident who needed thrusts must be checked by the nurse.

scoring.modelReasoning: A forceful cough with speech is mild choking: air is moving, so the aide stays, encourages the cough and watches, and does not slap, thrust, sweep or give water. When the cough goes silent and he cannot speak, with his hands at his throat and blue lips, it is severe: shout for help so the nurse and emergency team come while staying with him, then repeated cycles of 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts (AHA 2025) until it comes out. If he goes limp: lower him to the floor, start CPR with compressions, and look in the mouth before breaths, taking out only what can be seen. Afterward the nurse must check him; the aide reports what was seen, done and heard in objective words and writes it down.

fiveAndFive.ask: While the nurse is on her way: how many back blows before you switch to abdominal thrusts?

choices.label: Five, then five thrusts, and repeat
Keep slapping until it comes out

fiveAndFive.explain: The 2025 AHA guideline: repeated cycles of 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts until the object comes out or the person becomes unresponsive. Earlier courses taught abdominal thrusts alone.
